# Identification kit

**Generated by `npm run idkit` from `scripts/lib/identification-kit.mjs`. Do not edit by hand.**

The one source of every block a flow uses to mint, claim, update or resolve an identifier
([IDENTIFICATION_SYSTEM.md](../../../reference/identification/IDENTIFICATION_SYSTEM.md) §8). Each file is
a scope for the flow designer's clipboard: open the flow, select the step after which the block belongs,
and paste.

## Paste rules every block obeys (B1)

- No variables. A pasted scope cannot declare one, so every value is a Compose, evaluated once per run.
- No Until loop and no Filter array. Retries are flat attempts: attempt *k* runs only if attempt *k-1* failed.
- Every SharePoint write that must not lose a concurrent change is an HTTP MERGE with `IF-MATCH` (B9).
- No list is addressed by title or a hard-coded GUID, except Flow Configuration, which holds the bindings.
- The Request ID is always `guid()`. A client value is kept only as `clientCorrelationId`.

## Blocks, in paste order

| File | Block | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `00-identity-header.designer-paste.json` | Identity header | Reads the dataset bindings and ENVIRONMENT_CODE from Flow Configuration, sets the environment prefix (Z outside production, and Z if ENVIRONMENT_CODE is missing), and mints the Request ID. Every other block needs it, so it is pasted first, once per flow. |
| `01-claim-registry-reference.designer-paste.json` | Claim a Registry Reference (NITDA-YYYY-NNNNN) | Mints the record's Entity Key and claims one number from the NITDA counter in up to 10 flat attempts, then answers 503 RETRY_LATER if every attempt failed. Output: Compose_EntityKey_Record and Compose_Claim_Registry ({ ok, year, first, last, references }). |
| `02-claim-task-references.designer-paste.json` | Claim Task References (TASK-YYYY-NNNNN), single or bulk | Claims as many task numbers as the request has tasks (body tasks[], or 1) in one counter update, and hands them out in order. Output: Compose_Claim_Task.references[]. |
| `03-claim-file-reference.designer-paste.json` | Claim a File Reference (FILE-YYYY-NNNNN) | For DYNAMIC_ACTIONS open_file: mints the registry file's Entity Key and claims one FILE number. |
| `04-case-reference.designer-paste.json` | Draw a Case Reference (CASE-XXXXXX) | Draws CASE- plus 6 characters from the unambiguous alphabet with rand(), checks SUPPORT_CASES for a collision, and redraws up to 5 times. Any reference sent by the client is ignored. Output: Compose_CaseRef_Case. |
| `05-guarded-update.designer-paste.json` | Guarded Update (Rev + IF-MATCH) | Applies the request's changes to a TASK_QUEUE row with IF-MATCH, bumping Rev, in up to 3 flat attempts that each re-read the row. Copy it for any governed list by changing the dataset and the changes expression. Output: Compose_Updated_Task ({ ok, revAfter }). |
| `06-void-registry-row.designer-paste.json` | VOID row for a claimed Registry Reference | Runs when the record write fails after a claim (set its run-after to the record write: has failed). Writes the register's required columns as owner decision Q2 (3 October 2026) set them: Title VOID, ReferenceId = the claimed number, Status void, SenderEmail, plus VoidReason and IdState VOID, so the number is accounted for. |
| `07-client-request-hash.designer-paste.json` | Repeat-request check (ClientRequestHash) | Before creating anything for a Folio action, looks for a row created from the same action in the last 7 days. When Compose_Replay_Task is not null, the flow returns that row unchanged. |
| `08-resolve-target.designer-paste.json` | Resolve a target (Entity Key, else spo: locator) | Classifies the request's target as an Entity Key or an spo:<listGuid>/<itemId> locator on a bound dataset. Anything else is unresolved, and the flow answers 400 TARGET_UNRESOLVED. A bare item ID, RefIDD or title is never accepted. |

`00-identity-header` goes first, once. The others go where the flow needs them. Two blocks in one flow
need different tags; tags are set when the kit is generated, so ask for a variant rather than renaming
actions by hand.
